rules.title: impl of a foreign private trait is an error
rules.statement: In `impl Trait for T`, if `Trait` resolves to a trait that is not accessible from the impl site (not pub, or module-only and outside its module), the impl is rejected (privacy error). The check fires at the impl site that introduces the foreign trait name.
rules.divergence: Note: §4 module/package visibility model; trait must be pub-accessible to be implemented across package boundaries.

rules.title: impl of an undeclared trait is an error
rules.statement: `impl Trait for T` requires `Trait` to be a declared trait, except for the built-in marker traits `Copy` and `Drop`, which are always implementable by name without a visible trait declaration; any other unknown trait name is an error.
rules.divergence: Copy and Drop are treated as compiler built-in marker traits resolvable by name alone (not requiring import/dependency-graph visibility).

rules.title: impl-level generic params come from the impl header
rules.statement: An impl's own generic parameters are taken from `impl<...>`: for a trait impl `impl<T> Trait for U<T>` from the impl-type-params position, and for an inherent impl `impl<T> U<T>` from the standalone type-params position. These params (and their lifetime params and outlives bounds) are in scope for the target type, trait args, and all method signatures.

rules.title: where-clause outlives bounds augment impl params
rules.statement: Lifetime-outlives bounds (`'a: 'b`) and type-outlives bounds (`T: 'a`) written in an impl's where-clause are collected in addition to those in the `impl<...>` header and attached to the matching impl type parameter.

rules.title: Self binds to the impl target type
rules.statement: Within an impl, `Self` denotes the target type: for a concrete specialization (`impl U<i32>`) the fully resolved type with its type args; for a generic impl (`impl<T> U<T>`) the type with TypeVar args (including the type's lifetime params); for a blanket impl (`impl<T:B> Trait for T`) the TypeVar `T`; for a primitive target the primitive type.

rules.title: impl target unfolds transparent type aliases
rules.statement: When the impl target names a non-generic, non-lifetime-parameterized type alias, the alias is unfolded so the impl's methods register under the aliased concrete type's name (struct/datatype name, or its mangled concrete name when the alias carries type args; slice type string for a slice alias).

rules.title: impl for reference types
rules.statement: `impl Trait for &T` / `&mut T` is permitted; `&[T]`/`&mut [T]` canonicalize to the fat-pointer slice form and register under the same `$slice$<elem>` key as `impl Trait for [T]` (binding Self to the unsized-slice type); a generic ref-blanket `impl<T> Trait for &T`/`&mut T` keys under a fixed `$ref_$T`/`$mut_ref_$T` sentinel, restricted by coherence to one such impl per trait/ref-shape.
rules.divergence: Note: receiver-shape mangling is a Logos dispatch-implementation detail; observable rule is which reference forms are valid impl targets and that &[T] ≡ [T] for dispatch.

rules.title: impl for bare unsized self-types
rules.statement: `impl Trait for [T]`, `impl Trait for dyn Foo`, and `impl Trait for str` are permitted: the bare unsized slice / dyn-trait / str self-type is resolved in unsized-OK context, binding Self to UnsizedSlice / UnsizedDyn (and `str` to UnsizedSlice<u8>) so `&Self` canonicalizes to the corresponding fat pointer.

rules.title: impl for tuple types
rules.statement: `impl Trait for (A, B, ...)` is permitted; the empty tuple `()` is treated as the unit/void target. A variadic form `impl<A...> Trait for (A...)` covers tuples of any arity; otherwise the impl is keyed by arity (with element types when monomorphic).

rules.title: impl for fn-pointer covers all fn-ptrs of an arity
rules.statement: `impl<A,B,C> Trait for fn(A,B)->C` is permitted; because fn-pointers are type-erased to a uniform pointer at the Logos ABI, the impl covers every fn-pointer of the given arity and its methods are collected non-generically (one shared codegen, keyed by arity).
rules.divergence: Logos additive behavior: fn-ptr impls are arity-keyed and non-generic due to fn-ptr type erasure (no per-signature monomorphization).

rules.title: trait type args bind the trait's parameters
rules.statement: For `impl Trait<X> for U`, the trait's positional type arguments are resolved and bound to the trait's declared type parameters (e.g. `impl Into<i32> for C` binds the `Into` parameter to `i32`), making them available in method signatures. Lifetime arguments at trait position (`impl Trait<'a>`) are collected separately and not treated as type args.
rules.divergence: Note: Logos does not track regions structurally for trait dispatch; trait-position lifetime args are skipped from type-arg resolution.

rules.title: distinct blanket impls keyed by bound trait
rules.statement: Blanket impl methods register under a synthetic key incorporating the implemented trait, the bound trait, and the target typevar (`$blanket$Trait$Bound$T`), so two blankets of the same trait over different bounds (e.g. `impl<X: Primitive> Tr for X` vs `impl<X: PodRef> Tr for X`) register separately and do not collide with `T::method` lookups on unrelated generics.

rules.title: trait-impl methods inherit trait accessibility
rules.statement: Methods in a trait impl take their accessibility from the trait: if the trait is reachable, its impl methods are public (forced is_pub). `pub fn` is disallowed inside trait/trait-impl blocks. Methods of an inherent impl (no trait) keep their explicit pub/private status.

rules.title: self receiver parameter type defaults to a reference to Self
rules.statement: A method receiver parameter with no written type (`self` / `&self` / `&mut self`) has parameter type a reference to Self, mutable iff the receiver is declared mut.
rules.uncertainty: Derived from the visibility-promotion re-walk of params; the primary signature construction is in collect_fn.

rules.title: An impl whose target is one of its own type parameters is a blanket impl
rules.statement: A trait impl whose target type equals one of the impl's own type parameters (`impl<T: B> Trait for T`) is a blanket impl. The parameter's first bound becomes the impl's bound trait, and its associated-type equalities together with any additional bounds (and their associated-type equality clauses) are recorded, so the blanket can be instantiated at call sites on any concrete type satisfying those bounds.
